items.title: No local measure of prophylaxis adherence
items.whyItMatters: The unit sees only failures; adherence among patients who did well is unknown.
items.opportunity: Read records of controls from the same lists to estimate adherence and its association with rescue treatment.

items.title: Confounding by duration, opioids and illness
items.whyItMatters: Longer, more painful operations attract more prophylaxis and more nausea, which can hide or reverse an association.
items.opportunity: Match on operating list and adjust for duration, opioid dose and risk score.

items.title: Over-prophylaxis harm is unmeasured locally
items.whyItMatters: Extra agents may sedate patients and delay discharge (c4).
items.opportunity: Record sedation delaying discharge for all sampled patients as a second outcome.

items.title: Patients with limited English may be scored and counselled less
items.whyItMatters: The risk score includes history taken at the preoperative visit; missing history may lower the score.
items.opportunity: Record interpreter use and missing risk-factor history, and report adherence by it.

errorsFound: The need's 'one patient in eight' comes from the nausea log, which misses some rescue treatments at busy times (c3); case numbers may be slightly underestimated.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a matched case-control study with two outcomes and adjustment for the main confounders.
summary: Four gaps; missing local adherence and confounding are high severity.
